Hi Sophia — I pulled your sample traces and ran them through our trace-profiling harness. Below is a compact recommendation + the numbers we used. If you want the full CSV I attached the summarized kv_cache_profile.csv and a short runbook.

Assumptions and measured numbers (70B family, causal LM architecture):
- KV cache memory footprint: roughly linear in context length.
  - fp16 mode: ~0.95 GB per 1k tokens (includes key+value tensors + allocator overhead for our runtime).
  - int8 dynamic mode: ~0.55 GB per 1k tokens (quantization reduces KV tensor storage; we saw ~42% reduction on your traces).
- Typical session (6k tokens): fp16 ~5.7 GB, int8 ~3.3 GB.
- Peak session (40k tokens): fp16 ~38 GB, int8 ~22 GB.
- Model params resident memory (model weights/resident activations): doubles depending on quant: fp16 ~28–30 GB, int8 ~18–20 GB for a 70B open variant using our condensed kernel path.

Sizing guidance (steady 6 qps, target p95 latency 1.2s):
- Option A (fp16 for best quality): recommend 4 x H100-80GB GPUs in a pool (each GPU can host ~2 concurrent 6k sessions with room for KV and headroom; autoscale + 1 standby). This supports steady load with capacity for short bursts when combined with small autoscale knobs.
- Option B (int8 optimized): recommend 3 x H100-80GB (or 4 x A100-80 depending on availability) — int8 lowers per-session footprint so packing improves; expect ~25–30% lower GPU count vs fp16 for your workload.
- Burst handling: allow autoscale policy to add +2 GPUs for short windows (20 qps burst); if burst latency is strict, enable prefix caching to reduce token compute on repeated contexts.

Tradeoffs and risk notes:
- Int8 (dynamic/delivery quant) saved ~40% memory in our runs but you must validate output quality on your prompt set. For many RnD tasks it's acceptable, but for edge-case numeric fidelity tasks you may want fp16.
- KV cache spikes (40k tokens) can force model sharding or per-request fallback to smaller context variants. We recommend a per-customer limit on max context for active sessions and an archival mechanism for older context slices.
- Warm-up/throughput: int8 sometimes yields slightly higher throughput for tokens due to reduced memory traffic, but kernel availability can depend on driver and cuDNN/cuGraph stack — our default recommendation is H100-optimized kernels.

Concrete configuration we will propose in the quote:
- Dedicated pool: 3 x H100-80GB (primary) + 1 x H100-80GB standby for failover (int8 preferred after you sign-off on quality).
- Network: intra-pool NVLink enabled nodes (where available) + cross-AZ redundant head nodes.
- Software: Redwood runtime with KV-prefetch, prefix cache enabled, and canary route to fp16 variant for a small % of traffic.

Next steps: Sophia — can you run the attached 100-sample eval we included in the Drive link against the int8 build and send a small diff report on quality (ROUGE/EM/whatever metric you prefer)? If that looks good we'll finalize the Dedicated quote and SLA.

Attachments: kv_cache_profile.csv (summary), Draft_SLA_Helio_v1.docx
